question: Are the pages sr-extract flagged as possible JS-rendered shells actually shells?
method: Rendered each flagged page in headless Chrome via _tooling/sr-bridge.mjs and compared main.innerText length against the static-capture textChars recorded in content-inventory.json.
conclusion: No page is a shell. Rendered text tracks the static capture closely and no SPA mount point exists on any page. The renderRisk heuristic scores script-bytes-to-text ratio, and this WordPress/EyeCarePro theme ships ~140KB of Google Tag Manager and plugin script on every page, which inflates the ratio on genuinely short pages. C05 therefore reports a false positive that no re-run can clear, because sr-extract recomputes renderRisk from the static HTML alone and consumes no browser capture.
